research.summary:
Verdict: all buildable logic and data can be native C++ (text, reviewable on Linux). The Unreal editor is needed only as build/package host and for binary assets (meshes, textures, materials), which can be script-generated or partly avoided.

FactoryGame headers are public at the owner's SDK pin d2162c99, which equals master HEAD today. UFGBuildingDescriptor, UFGRecipe, UFGSchematic, UFGUnlockRecipe, UFGBuildCategory/SubCategory, AFGBuildable and AFGBuildableHologram are ordinary UCLASSes whose EditDefaultsOnly fields a subclass constructor can set. SML 3.12.0 accepts native classes: it discovers native UGameWorldModule subclasses (bRootModule), resolves /Script/ owners, and RegisterSchematic auto-registers recipes and their products. There is no register-buildable API.

Existence proof: Teleport Logistics (MIT, SML 3.12.0, CL502094, approved on SMR, 1,519 downloads) does all of it in C++, including Slate UI and RPCs. Its only assets are meshes/textures/materials imported by an editor Python script; no Blueprints, no GameFeatureData. Its repo lists retail checks as pending.

Costs: AFGBuildable::mIsUseable and mInteractWidgetSoftClass are private, so an AccessTransformers Friend entry is needed (SDK-wide rebuild). Native unlocks do not render in reward/MAM UI; two mods swap in stock BP unlock classes at runtime. Avoid asset loads in constructors. Docs demand FGColoredInstancedMeshProxy but the shipped mod uses UStaticMeshComponent (unresolved).

Editor workload for a custom mesh: build Development Editor once, run one Python import script, Alpakit package. No Blueprint or UMG authoring. The SDK uproject enables PythonScriptPlugin and EditorScriptingUtilities; whether the access-controlled CSS engine binary ships them is unverified.

Use a plain plugin (Alpakit Library template), not GameFeature: GameFeatureData is an editor-made asset needed only for icon libraries, user settings, ADA messages and input contexts.

On the Linux VPS only an engine-independent logic core can be compiled and tested (g++ -std=c++20 with sanitizers, as Teleport does); UObject glue cannot.

SMR requires AI-usage disclosure. Prior art exists: Circuitry (FicsitWiremod), 195k downloads, no licence.

claims.statement: FactoryGame headers ARE publicly browsable: 2,032 files live under Source/FactoryGame in the SDK repo at the owner's pinned commit d2162c99 (commit message 'Update headers to CL502094', 2026-08-11). master HEAD resolves to the same SHA as of 2026-10-13, so the 'compare with main' step is identical for every file I read. The Private/*.cpp files are generated skeletons, not game source, so behaviour must be inferred from headers/docs/other mods. The repo is GPL-3.0 at repo level and each header carries a Coffee Stain copyright line.

claims.statement: Every content type in the buildable chain is a plain native UCLASS whose EditDefaultsOnly members a derived C++ constructor (CDO) can set: UFGBuildingDescriptor::mBuildableClass; UFGItemDescriptor::mDisplayName/mDescription/mSmallIcon/mPersistentBigIcon/mCategory/mSubCategories/mMenuPriority; UFGRecipe::mIngredients/mProduct/mProducedIn (soft class list); UFGSchematic::mType/mTechTier/mCost/mUnlocks (Instanced); UFGUnlockRecipe::mRecipes (class is abstract, so a concrete native subclass is required); UFGBuildCategory and UFGBuildSubCategory (concrete UCLASS, fields mDisplayName/mMenuPriority/mCategoryIcon); AFGBuildable::mHologramClass/mDisplayName/mDescription (public); AFGBuildableHologram and AFGFactoryHologram (concrete UCLASS, usable as-is). The official tutorial builds them as Blueprints, but nothing in the headers requires that.

claims.statement: SML 3.12.0 content registration accepts native classes. (a) FPluginModuleLoader::FindRootModulesOfType discovers native UGameWorldModule/UGameInstanceModule subclasses (not only Blueprints) and reads bRootModule from the CDO, so a C++ class with bRootModule=true in its constructor is a valid root module (one per mod per module type, otherwise a Fatal log). (b) Content owner resolution explicitly handles the /Script/ mount point (native classes) by mapping module to plugin. (c) UGameWorldModule::mSchematics (TArray<TSubclassOf<UFGSchematic>>) is registered in the INITIALIZATION phase; RegisterSchematic auto-registers unlocked recipes and their products/ingredients as items. (d) There is no RegisterBuildable: a building becomes known because its descriptor is a recipe product. (e) Registration freezes at BeginPlay. Docs call UModContentRegistry a game-instance subsystem but the header derives from UWorldSubsystem (header wins).

claims.statement: Existence proof that the full chain can be native C++: Teleport Logistics (josh-tf, MIT, v0.5.12, built for CL502094 / SML 3.12.0 / UE 5.6.1) defines build category, sub-category, six building descriptors, recipes, UFGUnlockRecipe subclasses, two UFGSchematic milestones, a UGameWorldModule and UGameInstanceModule, buildable actors (hologram AFGFactoryHologram), power/belt/pipe connection components and an interaction widget, all in C++. Its only editor-authored content is ~35 mesh/material/texture .uasset files; it has no Blueprint assets and no GameFeatureData. It is live on SMR (4 approved versions seen, 0.5.12 approved, targets Windows + WindowsServer, 1,519 downloads at query time). Caveat: the repo is about a month old and its own validation.md lists the retail-game acceptance checks as pending, and Linux dedicated server is 'not certified'; this proves feasibility and SMR acceptance, not production quality.

claims.statement: Pure-C++ buildables need Access Transformers: AFGBuildable::mInteractWidgetSoftClass and the bitfield mIsUseable sit under 'private:' (line 1023 onward of FGBuildable.h), so a C++ subclass cannot set them directly. Teleport Logistics solves this with 'Friend' transformers on AFGBuildable/AFGBuildableFactory in Config/AccessTransformers.ini, then assigns mIsUseable/mInteractWidgetSoftClass/mHologramClass in its constructor. Friend and Accessor transformers need a C++ rebuild, and that repo warns changing them can force an SDK-wide rebuild, so list every needed private member up front. Whether the Accessor form works on a bitfield is untested (Friend is the proven route).

claims.statement: Editor-side automation is available in principle: the SDK's FactoryGame.uproject (at the pinned commit) enables PythonScriptPlugin and EditorScriptingUtilities, and DefaultEngine.ini carries a PythonScriptPlugin settings section. The Unreal Python API can import meshes/textures (AssetImportTask with FbxFactory), create assets via AssetTools.create_asset, and create Blueprints with BlueprintFactory.parent_class; scripts run from the command line with -ExecutePythonScript (full editor) or -run=pythonscript (commandlet). Teleport Logistics' scripts/import-assets.py does exactly this inside the CSS editor to produce all its cookable assets from OBJ/PNG sources. Python is documented as Experimental in 5.6.

claims.statement: Plugin mod vs GameFeature mod: the Starter Project and docs now default to GameFeature mods since SML 3.12/game 1.2 ('99% of mods'), but a GameFeature mod needs one editor-authored FGGameFeatureData asset (created by the Alpakit wizard through AssetTools.CreateAsset; named exactly the mod reference) and must live under Mods/GameFeatures. Alpakit also ships non-game-feature 'Library (Advanced)' templates, and Alpakit marks 'GameFeature': true in the packaged uplugin only when the plugin sits under Mods/GameFeatures. A GFDA is required only to register FGUserSetting, FGMessage, FGIconLibrary and FGChildInputMappingContext (schematics/research trees/recipes can instead go through SML modules). Teleport Logistics and Circuitry repos contain no GameFeatureData asset at their content root (absence read from the git trees, not quotable) and are live on SMR. So a pure-C++ buildable mod can use a plain plugin; the GFDA/editor step appears only if sign icon libraries or ADA messages are added. SML 3.12.0 (2026-06-06, GameVersion >=491125) is the latest release.

claims.statement: Vanilla assets can be used from C++ by path with no shipped copyright content. Official docs: reusing base-game icons/meshes by referencing their paths does not include the game's files in the mod; redistributing extracted assets needs Coffee Stain permission. Teleport Logistics references vanilla ingredient descriptors with LoadClass on /Game/FactoryGame/... paths and sets recipe producer to the vanilla BuildGun by soft path (BP_BuildGun_C); the official tutorial says the recipe's ProducedIn must be FGBuildGun. I found NO Coffee Stain published policy and no clause in the SMR Content Policy about asset reuse, so beyond the docs' wording the licence position is unverified.

claims.statement: An interaction UI needs no hand-made UMG: a C++ subclass of UFGInteractWidget overrides RebuildWidget() and returns a pure Slate tree (SButton, SEditableTextBox, SComboButton, SScrollBox, FSlateColorBrush, FCoreStyle brushes, the vanilla font by path). The official tutorial instead uses a Blueprint widget (Widget_UseableBase) and the optional Widget_Window_DarkMode. Client-to-server changes (e.g. a threshold) must go through a player-owned Remote Call Object; docs say native RCOs inherit FGRemoteCallObject and are registered through UGameInstanceModule::RemoteCallObjects (works from a native module, as Teleport does). Guard widget code with IsRunningDedicatedServer(). A zero-UI alternative exists: vanilla AFGBuildableCircuitSwitch exposes SetSwitchOn(bool) as a BlueprintCallable UFUNCTION (usable as an actuator). Not verified: pixel-level look of Slate UI in retail game.

claims.statement: Publishing on SMR carries a mandatory disclosure that applies directly to an AI-written mod: the Content Policy requires an 'AI Usage Transparency' section stating the purposes of AI use in the mod or its content, explicitly including source code created by generative models; it also requires a 'Network Activity Transparency' section for any external network use. The live ficsit.app page is a JS shell, so the text was read from the smr-frontend source (commit 0b129362). C++ mods wait for automated approval (about 1 to 3 minutes per docs).

evidence.quote: the purposes for which any AI tools have been used in the creation of the mod or its content

claims.statement: Prior art in exactly the owner's idea: 'Circuitry - Logic gates and More' (SMR ref FicsitWiremod, Scordium/FicsitWiremod, v14.1.63 built for >=502094) offers logic gates, sensors and wiring, has 195,478 downloads, and ships Windows, WindowsServer and LinuxServer targets (so native logic mods do run on Linux dedicated servers). It is hybrid, not pure C++: about 193 .cpp, 295 .h and 1,439 .uasset files including 214 Build_* Blueprint assets, with gate logic in C++ classes that Blueprints reparent (e.g. AAND). The repo has no LICENSE file and GitHub reports licence null, so its code cannot be reused. This is a scope/novelty risk for a 'Redstone' mod, not a technical blocker.

claims.statement: What can be verified on the Linux VPS: only code with no Unreal includes. Teleport Logistics keeps an 'engine-independent' core header shared with standalone tests and compiles it with plain g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic plus ASan/UBSan, alongside Python validators for assets. UObject/AFGBuildable glue needs UHT and the engine headers (engine repo access-controlled) so it cannot be compiled or syntax-checked here; the same repo states native tests exercise SDK code and do not establish retail acceptance. Docs add that new C++ files should be created through the editor or carefully by hand because UBT must see them.

claims.statement: Gotcha: native unlock classes do not render in the game's unlock UI. Two independent mods work around it by instancing stock Blueprint unlock classes at runtime: Teleport Logistics replaces its native UFGUnlockRecipe subobjects with stock BP_UnlockRecipe (loaded at INITIALIZATION, pinned with TStrongObjectPtr because native CDOs may sit in the disregard-for-GC set), and the LaserRifle mod states a custom C++ UFGUnlockInfoOnly subclass 'draws nothing'. The recipes themselves unlock fine. The exact failure mode on CL502094 for a bare native UFGUnlockRecipe was not verified (only the authors' comments).

claims.statement: Docs and shipped practice disagree on the building mesh component: the official tutorial says a placed building needs an FGColoredInstancedMeshProxy with a mesh, while Teleport Logistics (approved on SMR) builds every part with a plain UStaticMeshComponent and sets customization flags (mAllowColoring, mAllowPatterning) on the buildable. Not resolved here; test painting and abstract-instance behaviour in game before committing to one.

evidence.quote: Make sure that your building has an FGColoredInstancedMeshProxy component and that a mesh is assigned to it.
auto *Component = CreateDefaultSubobject<UStaticMeshComponent>(Name);

claims.statement: Icons do not strictly need editor-imported textures: SML ships FImageLoadingUtil::LoadImageFromFile/LoadImageFromByteArray, which decodes PNG/JPG into a transient, root-set UTexture2D at runtime, and the Alpakit C++ template stages a raw Resources directory (+AdditionalNonUSFDirectories=Resources). Whether such a transient texture is acceptable for UFGItemDescriptor::mSmallIcon / build-menu icons on the client (and harmless on a dedicated server) is untested. Teleport Logistics instead imports its icons as Texture2D assets.

evidence.quote: /** Loads image from file at the given path */

claims.statement: Constructor asset-loading hazard: because the engine runs a constructor for each spawned building (not only the CDO), a blocking LoadObject in the constructor can stall the game thread; Teleport Logistics measured a 2.3 s single-frame flush and now caches each path once (TStrongObjectPtr) so only the CDO's construction loads. Treat 'set defaults in the constructor' as safe for plain data, but cache any asset resolution.

Forgetting to set mHologramClass on the buildable crashes the build gun on selection, so it must be set in the constructor.

claims.statement: Assets a custom-mesh buildable cannot avoid (as authored data): a UStaticMesh, and for mesh texturing either the vanilla factory material MI_Factory_Base_01 referenced by path (the mesh's UVs must map to its atlas; the docs say you need to do that UV work yourself for your own models) or a custom material, plus optional icon textures. Teleport Logistics generates its meshes with Blender scripts (OBJ), binds native factory materials and falls back to /Engine/BasicShapes primitives before import. Whether engine primitives are cooked into a packaged client/LinuxServer when no mesh is imported is unverified, as is the retail look of such a fallback.

openQuestions: Does the access-controlled CSS engine release 5.6.1-css-83 ship PythonScriptPlugin and Python 3.11 binaries? (SDK uproject enables them; no direct check possible.)
Do native UFGSchematic/UFGUnlockRecipe classes show a correct HUB/MAM reward UI on CL502094 without swapping in stock BP_UnlockRecipe? Only two mods' comments were found, no CSS/SML statement.
Is a plain UStaticMeshComponent enough for Customizer painting and abstract-instance rendering, or is FGColoredInstancedMeshProxy mandatory (docs vs Teleport Logistics)?
Are /Engine/BasicShapes meshes available in packaged client and LinuxServer builds when a mod imports no mesh? Teleport only uses them as a pre-import fallback.
Can SML's runtime FImageLoadingUtil textures be used for UFGItemDescriptor::mSmallIcon / build-menu icons, and is the ImageWrapper module available on a dedicated server?
Does the Accessor access transformer work on the bitfield AFGBuildable::mIsUseable? (Friend is proven; Accessor is untested.)
Does a native-only buildable mod package and run cleanly for LinuxServer with the owner's toolchain? Teleport Logistics certifies Windows only; Circuitry ships LinuxServer builds but is hybrid.

Licensing: the SDK repo is GPL-3.0 with no visible exception, and I found no Coffee Stain policy on asset reuse; whether a mod linking SML/headers must be GPL, and any use of Minecraft's 'Redstone' name, was not assessed.

My search for native-content mods used gh search code and hit HTTP 403 rate limits partway, so the list is a lower bound. I found no buildable mod with zero .uasset files (Teleport Logistics still ships mesh/texture/material assets).
Teleport Logistics' retail acceptance checklist is marked pending by its author; how well its pure-C++ approach holds up in long multiplayer sessions is unknown.
recommendations: Architecture: put all signal/gate/latch/clock logic in an engine-independent C++ core (plain headers, no Unreal includes) tested on the Linux VPS with g++ -std=c++20 -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic and ASan/UBSan, as Teleport Logistics does. Keep the UObject/AFGBuildable layer as thin adapters that can only be compiled on the owner's PC.

Use a plain C++ plugin under Mods/<ModRef> (Alpakit 'C++ & Blueprint Library (Advanced)' template, no game feature) with a native UGameWorldModule subclass (bRootModule=true, mSchematics) and a native UGameInstanceModule; add a GameFeatureData asset only if sign icon libraries, ADA messages, user settings or input contexts become necessary.

Write the descriptor/recipe/schematic/unlock/category/buildable/hologram classes as native UCLASSes whose constructors set the defaults. Use AFGBuildableHologram or AFGFactoryHologram and set mHologramClass in every buildable constructor. Reference vanilla ingredients and BP_BuildGun by /Game/FactoryGame path (LoadClass / soft path) and cache every asset resolution (constructor hitch).

Decide all AccessTransformers.ini Friend entries before the first build (at least AFGBuildable for mIsUseable and mInteractWidgetSoftClass, plus any private member your gates touch), because each change forces a long SDK-wide rebuild on the owner's PC.

Plan the first vertical slice as one native buildable (for example a signal lamp or lever) + one schematic + recipe + Slate interaction widget + one RCO, with zero imported assets (engine primitives or vanilla meshes by path). Have the owner build and test it in game first: it settles open questions on unlock UI, mesh component, primitives and Linux packaging before the full gate set is written.

Editor-only steps on the owner's PC for a buildable with a custom mesh: (1) one-time Starter Project at the pinned commit (already done); (2) build the Development Editor target whenever headers, UCLASS layout or transformers change; (3) run one Python script (-ExecutePythonScript or commandlet) that imports OBJ/FBX meshes as UStaticMesh via AssetImportTask+FbxFactory and PNGs as Texture2D, with UVs authored to the vanilla factory material atlas (MI_Factory_Base_01); (4) Alpakit package for Windows + WindowsServer + LinuxServer (or UAT PackagePlugin); (5) in-game smoke test. No Blueprint, UMG, data-table or GameFeatureData authoring is required in this route.

For UI avoid UMG: subclass UFGInteractWidget, override RebuildWidget() with a Slate tree, send changes through a native FGRemoteCallObject, guard with IsRunningDedicatedServer(), and skip the widget path entirely for gates that can be toggled or cycled with E. Consider the vanilla power switch's SetSwitchOn as the first actuator.

Handle schematic reward UI deliberately: either accept an incomplete reward/MAM card for native unlocks, or copy Teleport Logistics' approach (swap in stock BP_UnlockRecipe at INITIALIZATION and pin it with TStrongObjectPtr) and test it on the owner's save.

Before publishing: prepare the SMR 'AI Usage Transparency' and 'Network Activity Transparency' text (source code is AI-generated; no network use), and decide the scope relative to Circuitry (195k downloads, no licence, so no code reuse) so the mod has a clear differentiator.

Do not treat Teleport Logistics as proven quality (its retail checks are pending) but as a structural template under MIT; re-verify every API name against the pinned headers before use and keep a written list of unverified items for the in-game test round.

verdicts.note: Re-read at d2162c99 (which is also master HEAD, committed 2026-08-11 'Update headers to CL502094', so the main comparison is trivially identical). (a) CONFIRMED: PluginModuleLoader.cpp calls FindNativeClassesByType plus FindBlueprintAssetsByTag and then checks 'if (ModModuleCDO->bRootModule)'. WorldModuleManager.cpp logs Fatal 'Only one root module is allowed' per plugin and module type. docs ModModules page: 'To make a C++-defined module a root module, set bRootModule = true; in its constructor', but it also says 'it is recommenced to make a blueprint child of it root instead'. verdicts.corrected: SML 3.12.0 accepts native content registration. FPluginModuleLoader::FindRootModulesOfType discovers native UGameWorldModule/UGameInstanceModule subclasses and reads bRootModule from the CDO. Setting bRootModule = true in the constructor is documented. One root module per plugin per module type, otherwise a Fatal log. The docs prefer a Blueprint child. Script-mount owner resolution maps /Script/<Module> to the plugin through the plugin descriptor's Modules list. mSchematics is registered in the INITIALIZATION phase. Schematic registration auto-registers the unlocked recipes and their products and ingredients as items, so there is no RegisterBuildable. Only the schematic and research-tree registries freeze (at BeginPlay), and the item registry never freezes. UModContentRegistry derives from UWorldSubsystem, although the docs call it a game-instance subsystem.

verdicts.note: CONFIRMED: FGBuildable.h at d2162c99 has 'private:' at line 1023; mInteractWidgetSoftClass (line 1039) and 'uint8 mIsUseable:1;' (line 1050) are both under it, both UPROPERTY. verdicts.corrected: A C++ AFGBuildable subclass cannot assign the private mInteractWidgetSoftClass and mIsUseable directly. The proven route is Friend access transformers (Teleport does this), which need a C++ rebuild and an SDK-wide rebuild when changed, so list every needed private member up front. mHologramClass is public and needs none. Runtime reflection (FindFProperty) is a plausible but untested alternative for these two UPROPERTYs. Accessor on a bitfield is untested.

verdicts.corrected: Pure-C++ buildables need access transformers for the private AFGBuildable members mInteractWidgetSoftClass (FGBuildable.h:1039) and the bitfield mIsUseable (:1050, under 'private:' from :1023). mHologramClass is public (after 'public:' at :813, set at :820) and needs no transformer. Three routes are in use by published mods: (1) Friend on AFGBuildable, used by Teleport Logistics and by Th3SMBuilder (Friend=(FriendClass="ATh3BuildableSM", Class="AFGBuildable"), then 'mIsUseable = true;' in the constructor, 2025-07 commit). (2) Accessor. Bidirectional Freight Platforms (approved on SMR, LinuxServer included) has `Accessor=(Class="AFGBuildable", Property="mInteractWidgetSoftClass")` and Accessors on the bitfields `uint8 mIsFullUnload : 1` and `uint8 mIsInLoadMode : 1`, and calls `self->SetmIsInLoadMode( false );` and `self->SetmInteractWidgetSoftClass( CustomWidget );` in BFPHooks.cpp. So Accessor on bitfields is demonstrably used; it is untested only for mIsUseable itself. (3) BlueprintReadWrite on both properties (mklierman HypertubeDestinations), which is BP-side and needs no C++ rebuild.
verdicts.note: Core verified at the pinned SDK: the private members, the Friend INI lines, and docs 'Friend and Accessor transformers require rebuilding C++ to take effect.' Corrections: (i) the 'untested' hedge on bitfield Accessor is superseded by the BFP evidence, which I pinned at BFP commit 09dce635 (2026-06-18). (ii) 'SDK-wide rebuild' is Teleport Logistics' own wording in docs/development.md. The official docs only say the header generator decides to rebuild 'based on the last changed date of the AccessTransformers.ini file', so touch the .ini after importing another mod's code. (iii) Open SML issue #226 notes the Accessor 'm' prefix quirk (GetmX/SetmX). No source contradicts the need for transformers.

The pinned FactoryGame.uproject has PythonScriptPlugin and EditorScriptingUtilities Enabled:true (lines 270-277), and DefaultEngine.ini:825 has the [/Script/PythonScriptPlugin.PythonScriptPluginSettings] section. verdicts.corrected: Starter Project and docs default to GameFeature mods since SML 3.12 / game 1.2: docs say '99% of mods should now include a "Game Feature Data Asset"', with the exception of mods that 'introduce no new content nor assets'. A GFDA is an FGGameFeatureData asset in the content root named exactly the mod reference (the ExampleMod GFDA is Content/ExampleMod.uasset). Alpakit's IsGameFeatureDLC matches plugins under Plugins/GameFeatures OR Mods/GameFeatures (not only Mods/GameFeatures) and then sets 'GameFeature': true in the packaged uplugin. Alpakit also ships non-game-feature 'Library (Advanced)' templates. The GFDA is mandatory only for FGUserSetting, FGMessage, FGIconLibrary and FGChildInputMappingContext (the docs also list FGSchematic, FGResearchTree and FGRemoteCallObject as scannable alternatives to SML modules). Plain plugins with content are live on SMR for CL502094 / SML 3.12: Teleport Logistics (no Content/<ModRef>.uasset; its Content root has no .uasset files at all) and Circuitry. Circuitry's SMR reference is FicsitWiremod (source: Scordium/FicsitWiremod; 'Circuitry' is a placeholder entry named 'Circuitry 2'). It has 195,480 downloads and v14.1.63 targets LinuxServer/Windows/WindowsServer, and its Content root has only CircuitryMap.uasset and HoldDelayed.uasset. SML 3.12.0 (2026-06-06, GameVersion >=491125) is the latest release.
verdicts.note: Quotes verified in the docs source and live docs. Basis for 'plain plugin works': the repo trees, the Alpakit Library templates, and the migration page's warning against having both a 'standard' and a 'game features' copy installed. I did not inspect the packaged uplugin's GameFeature flag, because that would mean downloading mod zips, which is outside the allowed actions. Absence of a GFDA in git is therefore not proof about the shipped package. Freshness: SML `dev` is 5 commits ahead of master (2026-10-12 'Update headers to CL513885', Wwise 2025.1.6.9117.4248). The docs `Dev` branch (2026-10-07) bumps Wwise from 2023.1.14 to 2025.1.6 and does not change the engine tag. So the CL502094 / Wwise 2023.1.14 pin will drift at the next game build. The Documentation master has no commits since 2026-08-05. Because the docs say 99%, defaulting to the GameFeature template is the safer option.

Verified at 47343693: `class TELEPORTLOGISTICS_API UTeleportLogisticsWidget : public UFGInteractWidget`, `virtual TSharedRef<SWidget> RebuildWidget() override;`, and `IsRunningDedicatedServer()` in the widget. SimpleInteraction.adoc uses Widget_UseableBase (BP). FGBuildableCircuitSwitch.h:46-47 shows `UFUNCTION( BlueprintCallable ...) void SetSwitchOn( bool isSwitchOn );`. Policy text verified at 0b129362, which is still the smr-frontend HEAD (2026-06-03). It states that mods must say 'the purposes for which any AI tools have been used in the creation of the mod or its content', lists 'If portions of the mod's source code were directly created by generative AI models', and has a separate Network Activity Transparency section. Live corroboration beyond the source: the api.ficsit.app Mod type exposes ai_use_disclosure{disclosure_type message} and network_use_disclosure. Teleport Logistics' live entry is type ai_usage ('Generative AI (Claude Opus 5, Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Astra) were used to create the models and source code.') and is approved. FicsitWiremod's is no_ai_usage. So an AI-written native mod passes SMR with the disclosure. The docs UploadToSMR.adoc says C++ mods wait for automated approval: 'about 1 to 3 minutes'. The policy exempts only ADA voice lines made via the documented WaveNet approach, and uncontrollable dependencies and dev tools.

verdicts.corrected: Engine-independent code (no Unreal includes) can be compiled and tested on this VPS with plain g++, as Teleport Logistics does (scripts/test.sh: `-std=c++20 -O1 -g -Wall -Wextra -Werror -pedantic -fsanitize=address,undefined` on Core/TeleportLogisticsScheduler.h and tests/transport_test.cpp, plus Python validators). UObject/AFGBuildable glue cannot be compiled here as the VPS is currently provisioned. That is a provisioning limit, not a fundamental one. Official docs (Development/Linux/LinuxSetup) and SML's own CI (LinuxCi: 'As of SML 3.12, we build binaries for SML and the custom Unreal Engine from Linux CI runners') document a full Linux modding environment (msvc-wine, wine, the UnrealEngine-CSS-Editor-Linux.tar.zst.* archive, Wwise). Teleport Logistics' scripts/build-linux.sh runs FactoryEditor build, the Python import commandlet, and Windows/LinuxServer packaging headlessly on Linux. The 5.6.1-css-83 release's Linux editor archive is about 8.3 GB compressed (4 parts), and this VPS's gh identity can list those release assets. The real blockers are the task's no-install rule and capacity (15 GB RAM total with about 2 GB available, 300 GB free disk, 8 cores). Manual C++ file creation is allowed but 'not recommended'; the docs warning is specifically about Visual Studio creating files in a temp directory that UBT cannot see.
verdicts.note: The Teleport Logistics quotes (-Werror -pedantic, 'Engine-independent rate budgets...', 'a passing report does not establish retail-game acceptance') are verified, which keeps the repo-derived parts at 'secondary'. The docs.ficsit.app quote 'you should not create new files from Visual Studio directly' is verified in Cpp/setup.adoc:229, but the 'must be created through the editor or carefully by hand' gloss is not what the docs say. They offer the editor wizard or manual creation ('very easy to make mistakes') followed by regenerating the VS project files. The UE engine repo is access-controlled via the Epic-GitHub link flow (dependencies.adoc). Also, TL's native automation tests run only in the editor ('Automation RunTests'), so functional verification of the glue needs an engine.
